steps.name: review
steps.detail: escalate: Policy flows compliant per audit, but core change applies edge filtering to a core UPLINK (OSPF) and uses inconsistent naming; inventory declares no edge_interfaces so scope is ambiguous. [medium] core: GigabitEthernet0/0 description UPLINK with router ospf 1 network 10.0.0.0/16: candidate adds inbound ACL FIX-IN (10 deny 23, 20 deny 445, 30 permit ip any any) to a core uplink, not a WAN edge. Operator asked to fix edge ACLs; applying edge filtering to a core link expands scope to critical routing adjacency. While 30 permit ip any any currently permits OSPF (IP proto 89), this introduces a new filtering point on a core link that was previously unfiltered. [low] core: New ACL named FIX-IN on core vs EDGE-IN on site-a and acl 3000 on site-b. Inconsistent temporary name will confuse next engineer; no cleanup/standardization to declared edge naming.

result.explanation:
site-a (IOS): adds seq 35 deny tcp eq 445; telnet deny and HTTPS via permit ip any already present.
site-b (VRP): adds rule 15 deny tcp eq 23; SMB deny and HTTPS permit already present.
core (IOS): creates ACL FIX-IN (10 deny 23, 20 deny 445, 30 permit ip any) bound inbound to Gi0/0.
NOT touched: only flagged interfaces changed; ssh/dns/http/ntp/snmp/bgp/https/rdp/ping unchanged, all flows compliant.
Risk: MEDIUM – new inbound filter on previously unfiltered core uplink.
ESCALATE per reviewer: edge filtering applied to core OSPF UPLINK expands scope; inconsistent name FIX-IN vs EDGE-IN/acl 3000, no edge_interfaces defined.

reasons: core: new inbound filter bound to GigabitEthernet0/0

review.summary: Policy flows compliant per audit, but core change applies edge filtering to a core UPLINK (OSPF) and uses inconsistent naming; inventory declares no edge_interfaces so scope is ambiguous.

concerns.text: GigabitEthernet0/0 description UPLINK with router ospf 1 network 10.0.0.0/16: candidate adds inbound ACL FIX-IN (10 deny 23, 20 deny 445, 30 permit ip any any) to a core uplink, not a WAN edge. Operator asked to fix edge ACLs; applying edge filtering to a core link expands scope to critical routing adjacency. While 30 permit ip any any currently permits OSPF (IP proto 89), this introduces a new filtering point on a core link that was previously unfiltered.
New ACL named FIX-IN on core vs EDGE-IN on site-a and acl 3000 on site-b. Inconsistent temporary name will confuse next engineer; no cleanup/standardization to declared edge naming.
